correctness.rationale: For T(j)=1 exactly at j=2, the empty set is an equilibrium and each nonempty equilibrium induces a 2-regular graph, so supports of positive size below 2g induce one cycle. A chord of a k-cycle forces k+2>=2g; a two-edge path between distinct cycle vertices through an external vertex forces k+4>=2g. Hence below 2g-4 each cycle is induced and every external vertex sees at most one producer. Cycle vertex sets give the asserted bijection, including the absence of positive supports below g and the multiplicity at g. The simple theta graph with path lengths g-2,g-2,2 has cycles of lengths g,g,2g-4, and the internal vertex of the short path blocks its unique long cycle. The one-cycle necessity excludes another support at that boundary. An independent bounded enumeration of cycles and profiles on the theta graphs g=5 through 9 agreed. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; its reported 16-graph run is finite corroboration only.

evidence: Gilboa–Nisan's cited result is a complexity result for the exactly-one pattern. The broader pattern/complexity works include different 0-allowed examples, and their inspected statements are not support enumerations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A classification of best-response patterns or the complexity of existence does not specify coefficients for each finite input graph. In particular, existence of the trivial profile says nothing about any positive coefficient.

evidence: Earlier exact polynomials are graph-family-specific; inspected general results concern pattern complexity. Neither supplies the two-edge obstruction or an all-girth counting theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The standard fact that producer components are cycles gives only a necessary condition. The no-external-shortcut argument supplies the decisive converse and the theta construction forces its failure at equality; these are the distinct parts of the result.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For the reviewed rule, equivalently the producer graph is 2-regular and no outside vertex has exactly two neighbors in the producer set. The zero-allowed pattern changes the status of the empty set and of external vertices with no producer neighbors, so results for it do not transfer.

originality.rationale: The same exact-two rule was previously treated on specific periodic graph families. The examined sources do not give or imply this initial coefficient law for all graphs of a given girth, or its universal sharp boundary. This is a statement-level conclusion bounded by the comparisons below, not a global priority claim.
residual_risks: Equivalent induced-cycle or graph fixed-point formulations may appear under different terminology. Unrelated web results provide no negative evidence; no universal historical priority is inferred.

value.rationale: The result converts a strategy-profile count into ordinary cycle counts over an entire sharp low-support range on arbitrary high-girth graphs. It identifies both the smallest positive support and its multiplicity. The exact cutoff explains why the local graph shortcut, not merely the possible appearance of unions of cycles, limits the correspondence.
